title: SCIM: Nested group traversal and staggered deprovision strategy for enterprise IdPs
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Problem: Large enterprise Identity Providers (IdPs) send SCIM group deltas that include nested groups and deep membership graphs. When deprovisioning users via SCIM, naively deleting direct memberships can cause cascading membership removals and unintended mass deprovision events. Current behavior: synchronous per-event processing that performs immediate membership removal and downstream RBAC changes, which has led to two near-miss incidents during AD/Okta sync storms.

Goal: Implement a safe, auditable, and reversible staggered deprovision workflow for SCIM group deletions that correctly resolves nested group membership, provides a dry-run/quarantine phase, integrates with audit logging and RBAC v2, and supports robust retry semantics for transient IdP errors.

Scope and constraints:
- Must work with existing SCIM webhook/event pipeline and the reconciliation job framework.
- Preserve per-customer isolation (Dedicated/Private customers may require different policies).
- Maintain audit trail for every staged action; linkable to Redwood Console timelines.
- Minimize user-visible disruption and support operator rollback within a configurable TTL.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Graph walk: On group deletion event, construct membership DAG (groups + nested groups + users) up to configurable depth, deduplicate nodes and compute user impact set.
2) Staged actions: produce a sequence of 3 staged intents per user: MARK_FOR_DEPROVISION -> QUARANTINE (soft remove from role evaluation but preserve account) -> FINALIZE (hard deprovision). Default stage timers: 48h quarantine TTL, configurable per-org.
3) Dry-run and notify: Before advancing from MARK_FOR_DEPROVISION to QUARANTINE, enqueue a dry-run summary to the org admins via Console notifications and create an audit record with the proposed delta.
4) Surge protection & batching: Use per-org rate limits and staggered, windowed processing to prevent sync storms from overwhelming the runtime. Backpressure to SCIM handler and exponential backoff with jitter on IdP 5xx responses.
5) Compensation and rollback: Support operator-triggered rollback that replays memberships from the last committed snapshot; tombstones with TTL for finalization to support audit and forensic queries.
6) Observability: Emit metrics: staged_deprovision_count, per-org pending_quarantine, finalize_rate, rollback_invocations, and include traces for each staged lifecycle in Console.

Implementation tasks (epics):
- Event DAG builder and membership dedup service (idempotent, cacheable)
- Staged intent datastore (tombstone + TTL semantics)
- Quarantine enforcement layer in RBAC v2 evaluation path
- Admin UX: dry-run summaries, manual approve/rollback flow in Console
- Retry/backoff orchestration and surge-protection
- Audit logging improvements: structured audit entries for every stage change and operator action

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests covering nested group graphs (depth >= 6) and cycles
- E2E test that simulates IdP sync storm with 10k membership changes without dropping below SLOs
- Console shows actionable dry-run and allows manual approve/rollback
- Audit log entries include operator id, event id, before/after snapshot hashes
- No regressions in existing SCIM reconciliation routes

Out of scope: full rework of SCIM delta model (separate RFC), per-provider custom remapping logic.
comments: 2026-03-09: Spike complete. Proof-of-concept DAG walker implemented in spike branch spike/eng/41987-membership-walk. Handles cycles via visited set and produces deterministic ordering.
2026-03-10: Design review with PM/Design. Agreed to default quarantine TTL=48h and allow org override. Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IDP/ENG-41987+Nested+Group+Deprovision
2026-03-11: Security review requested. Key concerns: ensuring audit immutability and preventing operator error during rollback. Security asked for HSM-backed audit checksums for finalization step.
2026-03-12: Implementation started. Created background job queue 'scim-staged-finalizer' and schema change PR. Code PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2758
2026-03-12: QA note: need a test org with complex nested groups (mirror of customer ACME corp fixture) to validate quarantine UX and notification surfaces.
steps_to_verify: Create test org with nested groups depth=6 using SCIM import
Trigger group deletion in IdP; verify 'MARK_FOR_DEPROVISION' intents appear in staged store
Use Console dry-run view to inspect impact and confirm notifications are generated
Advance a batch to QUARANTINE and verify RBAC evaluation excludes quarantined users
Finalize batch and confirm audit logs contain before/after snapshot hashes and operator id
Simulate IdP 5xx responses and verify exponential backoff + surge-protection keeps system within SLO
acceptance_criteria: Staged intents persisted and durable across process restarts
Quarantine enforces exclusion from RBAC v2 decisions without deleting user records
Operator can rollback within TTL and rollback is idempotent
Dashboards show per-org pending_quarantine and finalize_rate metrics
Automated tests for cyclic group graphs and deduplication pass in CI
